title: Design of a 13.56-MHz Capacitive Wireless Power Transfer Coupler with Auxiliary Inductive Coupling
content: Capacitive wireless charging for electric vehicles requires compensation of the large reactance associated with small coupling capacitances. We examine a 13.56 MHz capacitive coupler with auxiliary inductive coupling under static, aligned conditions. Each copper winding surrounds a cast-iron electrode and connects its inner terminal to the electrode, providing compensation inductance and magnetic coupling. External π matching networks complete the compensation. A five-loop formulation reduces the capacitive network to a two-port model for initial winding design. Full-wave simulations compare receiver assemblies and shield dimensions across a 50 mm electrode gap. Changing from a mirrored to a rotated receiver assembly increases the simulated ideal-matching efficiency limit from 43.96% to 91.01% at the design frequency. Increasing the shield side length from 150 to 300 mm reduces maximum sampled rear-side electric fields by 86.41–91.97% at the same 100 W incident power. A prototype is characterized using a vector network analyzer, and its measured S-parameters are used in matching and nonlinear circuit simulations. At 13.56 MHz, the circuit predicts 67.80 W DC output from 97.74 W DC input, giving a DC–DC efficiency of 69.36%. These results provide an aligned design basis for further investigation of matching bandwidth and displacement tolerance in vehicle charging.
